newsitem.title: CHINA: Southern China urged to boost corn cultivation.
newsitem.headline: Southern China urged to boost corn cultivation.

text.p: Provinces in southern China should boost the amount of land used to grow corn in order to meet rising demand, the Futures Herald said in an edition seen in Beijing on Friday.
Eight provinces and cities in southern China buy millions of tonnes of corn from other provinces annually, the newspaper quoted agriculture expert Lu Ming as saying.
Therefore, southern China must increase land under corn, Lu said. He did not elaborate. The newspaper gave no details on Lu Ming, describing him only as an agriculture expert.
A livestock industry boom in recent years has boosted demand for corn.
Demand for feed grain alone was expected to total 160 million tonnes in the year 2000, the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
China produced 111.99 million tonnes of corn in 1995, accounting for 24.1 percent of total grain output.
